tagline: A CAIO-facing console that connects org structure, the human and agent workforce, Quality Procedures, processes, AI initiatives, harness engineering, D2D delivery, value realization and token economics into one product.

hero_stats.label: entity types in the mock data model

challenge.description: Most AI dashboards show adoption. The requirement here was to show the whole transformation chain — organization to job to activity to Quality Procedure to process to human/agent allocation to AI initiative to agent harness to D2D delivery to performance to value realization to token economics to strategic outcome — as one connected, navigable product rather than a set of disconnected screens.

stats.label: governed agents with digital job descriptions

phases.title: Scaffolded and re-stacked
phases.body: Started from the DAK template via `dak init`, then stripped it to this project's actual stack: React 19 + Vite + the Astryx/DEWA theme, frontend-only, no backend. Added recharts, @xyflow/react and dagre for the graph views, and TypeScript for the data layer.

phases.title: Design tokens and the route shell
phases.body: The DEWA radius scale and 48px pill buttons layered on Astryx, the Estimated/Observed/Verified/Validated value tag, and the full route table for all 16 modules — every route real and clickable from day one.

phases.title: The mock data model
phases.body: 24 entity interfaces, one seed file per entity in strict foreign-key order, and the requirements doc's formulas implemented once in lib/calc.ts. Verified by smoke script: exact required volumes, zero dangling foreign keys, and both worked examples reproducing the doc's own figures.

phases.title: Executive Overview
phases.body: All 16 KPIs and charts A–H, every number computed from the dataset rather than hardcoded, plus the Executive Attention Required panel.

phases.title: Organization
phases.body: Two graph views — the traditional org chart and an AI-native workforce network with agent-supervision edges — over five-dimension filters and a current/target agenticity toggle.

phases.title: Processes and Quality Procedures
phases.body: The process register with per-step ownership, contribution split and automation level, and the QP register with a compliance dashboard and the panel showing how a Quality Procedure converts into an agent-executable workflow.

phases.title: AI Initiatives and Agents
phases.body: The initiative portfolio as a table and an 11-stage Kanban, plus the Digital Employee Registry and a nine-tab Agent Profile covering the digital job description, process assignments, harnesses, performance, tokens, value, risk and audit history.

phases.title: Harness Engineering
phases.body: The Agent = Model + Instructions + Context + Knowledge + Tools + Workflow + Guardrails + Evaluations + Human checkpoints + Observability + Cost controls formula, and a visual Harness Designer whose 11 workflow blocks each open their real configuration.

phases.title: D2D Integration, Copilot and Workforce
phases.body: The 12-stage demand-to-delivery journey with a live per-stage demand count, and the deliberate separation of AI adoption from AI work contribution from AI business value — three different measures that are routinely conflated.

phases.title: AI Playbook
phases.body: A living playbook rather than a document: one scope resolver, one builder, and the same 15 sections re-derived for any of nine scopes — enterprise, division, department, section, job, process, Quality Procedure, agent, or strategic objective.

features.title: One graph, many lenses
features.description: The Enterprise Map is a single shared dataset with a pure lens function per view, never ten independent screens. The AI Playbook follows the same rule with one scope resolver and one builder.

features.title: Derive, never hardcode
features.description: Every displayed number comes from a formula in lib/calc.ts or an aggregate module reading real foreign keys. Seed gaps are filled at read time rather than hand-authored, so the worked examples fall out of generic rendering with no special-casing.

features.title: Every value is tagged
features.description: Benefits, costs, coverage percentages and released capacity all carry an Estimated, Observed, Verified or Validated tag, so an estimate is never read as a validated benefit.

features.title: Browser verification in the loop
features.description: Each module is clicked through in a real browser before it ships. That practice has caught rendering and seed-data defects that the type checker, the bundler and the unit tests all missed.
